commitResults.messageTitle: Clarify storage contracts and assignment fields
commitResults.messageBody:
The storage diagram uses a class label for the Storage interface and
does not show how optional assignments appear in participant JSON.

These omissions make the persistence boundaries harder to follow.

Use interface notation, label the actual references and multiplicities,
and show nullable assignment strings on the participant adapter.
Keep low-level I/O helpers outside this stable overview so the diagram
can be reviewed independently of the safe-saving implementation.

Saving creates the destination before taking a participant snapshot.

A failed snapshot can therefore leave an empty first-save file.

Add regressions that require a failed snapshot to leave a missing
destination absent and preserve an existing file byte for byte.

commitResults.messageTitle: Protect participant files during failed saves
commitResults.messageBody:
Participant saves write directly to the destination after creating it.

An interrupted write can truncate the last saved data, and a failed
first snapshot can leave an empty data file.

Serialize before file creation, stage and flush the complete content,
and require atomic replacement. Keep a recovery copy until replacement
succeeds so a failed restore can leave the old bytes recoverable.

Add deterministic failure tests for staging, backup, replacement,
recovery and cleanup. Preserve read errors, the JSON schema and every
participant field without promising an in-memory rollback.

The persistence guides do not explain failed saves or recovery files.

Users and maintainers need to distinguish protected on-disk data from
an in-memory command change and understand the limits of restoration.

Describe staged writes, atomic replacement, recovery and cleanup.
State the single-writer assumption and avoid claiming startup recovery
or protection against power loss and filesystem corruption.

commitResults.messageTitle: Report snapshot failures as save errors
commitResults.messageBody:
Snapshot construction can throw an unchecked exception after a command
changes the model.

The save boundary only wraps I/O failures, so these failures bypass the
normal user-visible save-error path.

Translate snapshot and serialization runtime failures into IOException
inside that boundary. Keep null precondition checks outside it and
preserve the original cause without logging participant contents.

Add a command-level regression for the error response, original file
bytes and already-applied model change.
